It’s Giving Wood: Inside The Sumptuous Walnut-Lined Connaught Grill

Ari Alibhai·
Food & Drink
·19 November 2026·4 min read
Share
6
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:19
Instaread

Ari visits bucket list restaurant (his and ours), The Connaught Grill to review and indulge…

I appreciate this won’t rank high on the list of issues that concern you, but the truth is, the number of restaurants I wish I’d been to has seriously diminished over the past couple years. This isn’t because I’ve somehow lost my love of lunch (which, for me, would be the equivalent of giving up on life itself). No, it’s thanks to the fact The Sauce has given me the chance to live my dream, and eat out as an occupation. That’s meant that the roster of places I haven’t visited, but really want to, keeps on getting eaten into, a bit like one of those sardine bait balls you see on Blue Planet, gradually disappearing until all you have left is a scattering of shiny scales. 

Unlike the sardines, though, part of my hitlist remains intact. And at the top of this gastrotree, for a while, has perched The Connaught Grill. I’d seen photos of the Grill post its 2020 renovation, but nothing prepared me for the sheer beauty of the restaurant’s walls and furniture, hand carved out of American black walnut by a team led by master woodsmith, Mira Nakashima.

Walnut carries natural fissures, which were apparent on the raw finished wooden panelling, which act as screens between tables to create semi-private booths. The splits are a large part of the beauty of this wood and Nakashima is famous for her technique of using butterfly joints to stabilise cracks in the walnut, embedding winged wooden inserts to bind the pieces together more strongly. I know I’ve spent longer than I should, on wood, but it’s key to the Connaught Grill experience. You basically feel like you’re eating inside the world’s most luxurious humidor, coddled and comforted by your surroundings.

I know I’ve spent longer than I should, on wood, but it’s key to the Connaught Grill experience…

So, to the food. It being November, there was only one option, from my perspective. The £147 six course game menu. This is peak game season, albeit not so much for grouse. Grouse tends to be a little tough and very gamey by mid-November. The Connaught’s solution was to substitute pigeon in its place, which transpired to be an inspired swap. 

We began with a foie gras tart. Rather than an individual tartlet, what arrived was a slice of what was clearly a substantial pie. It came with a scatter of hazelnuts and a little fig cooked down with Port to sharpen it up. The pastry was razor thin, the regal liver of the very highest quality. Rather than just smooth pâté, it was stuffed with generous chunks of the actual whole liver. And served with tall flutes of Billecarte Salmon Reserve Champagne. This is how I imagine Bertie Wooster would begin a long lunch at the Drones. It was decadent, rich as hell, and utterly unwilling to conform to modern mores.

It was stuffed with generous chunks of the actual whole liver…

I felt fortunate, as I ate the tart that we’d warmed up with a couple of cocktails. These were taken in the gorgeous cocoon of the Red Room Bar at The Connaught, before we’d arrived for dinner. My senses had been sharpened and my tastebuds whetted by a perfectly made gin martini. Then a frankly peerless Corpse Reviver Number 2. This gin/absinthe mash up is one of the great cocktails, when made correctly. Herbal, strong, sour, and cold as can be, it’s an ideal way to start a meal like this. 

Back to the menu. More radical and in my view, even better than the foie tart, was a smoked venison sausage with ceps and pearl barley. The sausage was meaty but relatively mild flavoured, which allowed the ceps some room to shine. Next followed our main, pigeon. A lean, brooding purple, rare breast sat in a red wine jus, with some bits and bobs of the bird to accompany it. None of which could compete with the perfection of the breast itself.

Pigeon is one of my favourite birds, when cooked rare, as it was here. Its marriage with the 2018 Gevrey-Chambertin by David Duband that arrived as part of the £110 wine pairing, is something I intend to reminisce about on the next occasion I’m unfortunate enough to have a less stellar lunch elsewhere. Other highlights from the wines included a magnificent, floral, delicate, lightly sweet 2019 Mosel Riesling by Egon Müller, poured from the magnum. 

Pigeon is one of my favourite birds…

There was, of course, pudding. Poached pear, which was underdone, with some twirls of cream and a cinnamon crumble. Far better was a simple slice of superlative, buttery, gubbeen. It’s an Irish semi-soft, washed rind cheese that arrived with a tiny, and happily, perfectly poached apple. We finished with a complicated cocktail, ‘The End Game’, which combined The Macallan 18, with coconut, pear eau de vie, ginger and mead, to create something that wasn’t as nice as a measure of Macallan with a drop of water would have been. But let me make this clear. The slightly hard pear and curious cocktail were tiny wrinkles on an otherwise faultless, seasonal and ambitious dinner. 

Find it: The Connaught, Carlos Place, Mayfair, W1K 2AL.
Click it: www.maybourne.com
‘Gram it: @theconnaught

Forget The Mountains, The Best Après Ski Is In London. Here’s Where To Find It…

Phil Clarke·
Food & Drink
·19 November 2026·10 min read
Share
12

Anyone knows that the second best thing about skiing (and quite possibly the first best) is the après-ski, the wine and melty cheese fuelled fun that takes over the moment you step off the slopes. As winter rolls around, alpine Europe reverberates to ’80s power ballads, Eurobeats and slurred drinking songs. The covid pandemic is widely believed to have been superspread after aprés skiers took to the tables of a Tyrolean bar to belt out AC/DC’s Highway to Hell, before dispersing to all corners of the globe, merrily viral shedding as they went. That’s how powerful après-ski is. In fact, it’s so popular that around this time of year a slew of bars and restaurants set out to recreate the apres ski phenomenon here in London.

Which means that you don’t need to jump on a shuttle to Geneva, take out a mortgage to buy a ski pass or go near a set of thermals. Well, maybe on the thermals. You just need to head to one of London’s excellent après-ski joints. And, it turns out, they’re popping up here, there and everywhere this autumn and winter. Here are some of our favourites…

The Stafford, St James’s

The cobbled courtyard at The Stafford has received a makeover and is channelling Aspen this winter. The Stafford has been a magnet to homesick Americans for over 80 years. Now they (and you) can head to the Rocky Mountains via Green Park tube station for a London après-ski experience.

The cobbled courtyard at The Stafford has received a makeover…

Take an igloo (we famously love an igloo) and order from the Aspen Feast Menu. The menu features ‘alpine-inspired’ sharing plates including cheese fondues along with comforting winter desserts. Try the Charcuterie and Alpine Cheese, Potato Rösti and Smoked Salmon, Baked Camembert or Truffled Cheese Fondue.

These are best washed down with an iconic Stafford Martini. And the only thing that could improve the experience would be to continue on and stay at the hotel!

Find it: 16-18 St James’s Place, St James’s, SW1A 1NJ
Click it: www.thestaffordlondon.com
‘Gram it: @thestaffordlondon

Clays, Soho (And The City & Canary Wharf)

Clays, London’s go-to for competitive socialising, has undergone a complete transformation this winter. It is now an après-ski destination with a twist.

London’s go-to for competitive socialising…

Not only have the venues taken on the appearance of snowy mountain scenes, the glamour of après-ski has spread to the drinks and the food.

Even the simulated clay shooting now takes place against a snowy mountain landscape and the games have received seasonal tweaks.

You can read all about the Clays Après Ski here. But make sure you check it out before spring arrives.

Click it: www.clays.bar
Find it: Various locations
‘Gram it: @clays_bar

The Beaumont, Mayfair

One of the smartest Euro ski destinations comes to one of the smartest London hotels this November in a meeting of minds that can only mean one thing. Fondue.

It’s fair to say that the traffic between Gstaad and Mayfair is pretty high this time of year. But save yourself a visit to the private jet terminal and instead go during November when après-ski will be in full swing thanks to a partnership with The Alpina Gstaad.

The two-week takeover until Sunday 29th November will see The Alpina’s Executive Chef Francesco De Bartolomeis presenting a menu celebrating traditional Swiss Alpine cuisine. So look forward to raclette, rösti and fondue in abundance.

Meanwhile Head Mixologist Konstantinos Peristeris who will be serving exclusive cocktails, including Apple Ski, blending apple eau-de-vie, apple and warming spices, and Sloe Motion, combining sloe gin, Chambord, Campari and Champagne.

Find it: 8 Balderton Street, Brown Hart Gardens, Mayfair, W1K 6TF
Click it: www.thebeaumont.com
‘Gram it: @thebeaumontldn

Wagtail, The City

We are famous for being incredibly partial to a London rooftop restaurant. And our search for après-ski in London Venns perfectly at Wagtail.

The rooftop restaurant is transformed this winter to celebrate the best après-ski traditions. So pull up a faux fur throw and let’s settle in. The rooftop’s two terraces are après ready, decked with twinkling lights, aforementioned throws and pine garlands.

The drinks partner for the event (all hospitality ‘activations’ come with drinks partners) is French vodka Grey Goose. Cue a series of cocktails which will have you coming back to the bar for more.

These consist of Chocolate Orange Espresso Martini Cocktail (Grey Goose (a given), creamy dark chocolate and orange liqueurs and espresso. Or a tantalising Tangerine Sour, a Christmas take (coz tangerine) on a classic, with Grey Goose, bianco vermouth, tangerine sherbet, lemon and honey. Finally, they hardly couldn’t include a Classic Vodka Martini Cocktail, made with (you guessed it) Grey Goose along with Carpano dry, and finished with a lemon twist, olive or briny pearl onion.

Find it: 68 King William Street, The City, EC4N 7HR
Click it: ww.etmcollection.co.uk
‘Gram it: @wagtailldn

Dovetale, Mayfair

From Wagtail to Dovetale, and another London après-ski . Or, to be precise, après tea.

Always one for a pun, I was delighted by the wordplay, but you’ll probably be more won over by the après themed tea. Brought to you by Executive Chef Leonel Aguirre, who recently joined from Head Cheffing Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO, the tea brings together all the classics.

The terrace has been given an alpine makeover, so you’ll feel ready from the moment the first tiered sandwich thing arrives. The menu includes a selection of fine teas, seasonal savoury bites and festive sweet treats, alongside cocktails with Woodford Reserve.

It’s an option but you should definitely try the warm Valrhona chocolate fondue to share.

Find it: 1 Dover Yard, Mayfair, W1J 8NE
Click it: www.dovetalelondon.com
‘Gram it: @dovetalelondon

Winter Wonderland, Hyde Park

Okay, unpopular opinion time… I think that people are warming to Winter Wonderland. Once seen as the scourge of Hyde Park Corner, a tourist trap that’s horribly overpriced and unpleasantly overcrowded, it’s still seen as all these things but now it’s part of the furniture. Like Jimmy Carr or Jeremy Clarkson, it’s somehow and unexpectedly gained national treasure status without anyone noticing. And, speak it softly it’s even… Rather fun.

After all, it has a great ice rink, a handy Christmas market and, now, an après-ski experience. The Après Ski Party Resort does pretty much what it says on the alpine tin. A village given over to festive drinks, bratwurst hot off the grill and live DJs. You even get to pay the same prices as you might in a Swiss resort.

Find it: Louisa Duckworth Walk, Hyde Park, W1K 7AN
Click it: www.hydeparkwinterwonderland.com
‘Gram it: @hydeparkwinterwonderland

Aqua Nueva, Soho

Perched on the edge of Soho, Aqua Nueva scales the side of one of those imposing Regent Street terraces like it’s the north face of The Matterhorn. From this rooftop vantage point you can see across Mayfair and, this winter, you can experience some après-ski luxury too.

The terrace has been given over to an après-ski theme with Casamigos Tequila (I know, it’s arguably off topic but all the best après-ski involves tequila). Welcome to Casa Montaña.

At the heart of the terrace sits the Casamigos Hut, an open-air winter cabin framed in pine garlands and twinkling lights. It’s lined with Casamigos’ signature turquoise mosaic pattern and comes with sofas piled with sheepskin throws and branded cushions.

There’s also a cocktail menu teeming with tequila-based cocktails which all look fabulous.

Find it: 30 Argyll Street, Soho, W1B 3BR
Click it: www.aquanueva.co.uk
‘Gram it: @aquanueva

Tewinbury Farm, Hertfordshire

Twenty-something minutes from Central London by train, Tewinbury is a firm favourite of The Sauce and it’s still a darn sight closer than the nearest ski resort.

Après-ski at Tewinbury is best enjoyed after a leisurely walk around the famous winter light trail. If you’ve not seen them, then do.

The next stop after the lights? The Après Ski Bar. And it’s got everything you’d want from après-ski So winter drinks, food and live music. And it’s on every night.

The vibe is intended to be less ski resort theme park, more somewhere warm to stay for another round once you’ve walked the woods. Turn up in your boots, then fill your boots. Not literally.

Find it: Hertford Road, Welwyn, Hertfordshire, AL6 0JB
Click it: www.tewinbury.co.uk
‘Gram it: @tewinburyfarmhotel

Gelupo, Soho

Can I tell you a secret? Please don’t tell Lottie, who just wrote our definitive guide to London fondue restaurants. I don’t like melted cheese. It makes me feel a little sick. However, I can gulp down chocolate fondue by the pint like it’s freshers’ week at the North Pole.

Which is where Gelupo comes in. Jacob Kenedy’s bustling Soho gelateria has opened its winter lodge, transporting guests to the Italian Alps. And it’s all about the dark chocolate fondue for two (or three, if you’re not there with me) to share. It comes served with bite-sized pieces of Forno Gentile panettone, mini scoops of gelato and slices of pear for dipping.

Meanwhile, the gelato has a seasonal flavour, quite literally, with the range expanded to include prune and Armagnac, chestnut and panettone.

There’s also après-ski drinks such as vin brulé, hot chocolate spiked with amaro or amaretto, and the brandy-laced Bombardino.

Find it: 7 Archer Street, Soho, W1D 7AU
Click it: www.gelupo.com
‘Gram it: @gelupogelato

Kitchen At Holmes, Marylebone

Looking for a new take on the whole après-ski thing? Kitchen At Holmes (which was one of Ari’s first reviews and still tops Google, by the way) has brought in an après-ski cinema.

They’ve teamed up with La Fromagerie to bring a taste of the Alps to Marylebone with a private rooftop cinema experience.

Along with some classic movies, you can enjoy cheese fondue (see above for my thoughts on that), mulled wine, and a festive dessert.

Find it: 83 Chiltern Street, Marylebone, W1U 6NF
Click it: Get tickets here…
‘Gram it: @holmeshotelldn

I’ve now written après-ski so many times it sounds like the name of a pretentious Russian and no longer feels like a real word, let alone a theme for some of London’s most enjoyable bars and restaurants!
